doc: Planetary targets (STANDARDS section 8, 10.9). Longitudes east-positive in [-180, 180). Every target carries the 10.9 fields: landing_class (landing_demonstrated | landed_tipped | candidate | future_mission), mission, year, outcome_note (one sourced sentence), outcome_source (its URL), center_note (how the centre was obtained; says 'secondary source' where the centre is not from a primary NASA/JPL/ESA/CNSA page or a paper opened by the team). Moon DEMs for the new targets are 6 km remote windows (pipelines/fetch_data.py window-clip). All status values are 'proposed' until the team lead approves. v1.2 (2026-11-14): Mars targets insight_elysium, spirit_columbia, zhurong, oxia_planum added; Moon targets apollo17_taurus_littrow, im1_odysseus, im2_athena, cabeus_b_peak, mons_mouton_plateau added. Jezero centre set to 18.4447, 77.4508 (NOT confirmed by NASA/JPL); Gale DEM is the extracted tile gale_ctx_dtm_tile_3_3.

moon_reference.official_list_date: 2024-10-28 (NASA release RELEASE24-136, read 2026-11-14; no coordinates given)
moon_reference.note: NASA lists them 'in no priority order'. Five have a PGDA 5 m DEM (see docs/data_notes.md for the other four).

sites.name: Haworth (NASA Artemis III candidate region)

center_source.how: DEM centre: centre pixel of the downloaded 5 m LOLA DEM raster (south polar stereographic, sphere radius 1737400 m), projected to lon/lat with pyproj by pipelines/fetch_data.py centre. Proxy only: the ROI file is not a real archive, and the DEM tile is not the landing region.

sites.notes: PGDA ROI name 'Haworth' (no site number). NASA list name 'Haworth' matches exactly.
sites.outcome_note: NASA named this region among nine candidate Artemis III landing regions, 'in no priority order', with no coordinates given; no landing has occurred.
sites.center_note: DEM-raster centre of the PGDA 5 m DEM (proxy, not a NASA landing coordinate).

center_source.how: ROI centre: centre of the bounding box of all 283 vertices of the Site11 ROI polygons (real gzip archive, shapefile with PROJCS .prj, projected to lon/lat on the 1737400 m sphere by pipelines/fetch_data.py centre). DEM-raster centre for comparison: -88.6835, -67.9341 (about 0.4 km apart).

sites.notes: DOUBT: PGDA lists two 'de Gerlache rim' DEMs: Site11 and SL2. Site11 chosen (Site number, its ROI file is real). SL2 (lola_5m_sl2_surf) is the alternative; the team lead decides. NASA name has 'Rim 2', PGDA has no rim number.

sites.name: Jezero crater: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance)

center_source.how: NOT CONFIRMED BY NASA/JPL. Value 18.4447, 77.4508 kept as set by the lead (4 decimals). Wikipedia article 'Octavia E. Butler Landing' (read 2026-11-14) gives 18.44 N, 77.45 E (rounded). The four-decimal values were seen only in a Wikipedia mirror in a search result (not opened). NASA pages read with no coordinates: mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/mission/where/, mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/timeline/landing/, science.nasa.gov/resource/jezero-crater-mars-2020-rover-landing-site/, nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-announces-landing-site-for-mars-2020-rover/. JPL press-kit pages returned HTTP 403.

sites.notes: Mars target 1. Centre is the landing site, not the crater centre (Jezero crater centre per Wikipedia 18.38, 77.58, not used). Lead decision: confirm the 4-decimal centre before publication.
sites.outcome_note: NASA: Perseverance landed in Jezero crater on Feb. 18, 2021, and Jezero was chosen as the landing site.
sites.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia 'Octavia E. Butler Landing' (rounded to 18.44 N, 77.45 E); the 4-decimal value 18.4447, 77.4508 is not confirmed by NASA/JPL.

sites.name: Gale crater: Bradbury Landing (Curiosity)

center_source.how: Coordinate of the landing site from the article's coordinate template (Wikipedia API prop=coordinates: -4.5895, 137.4417, globe mars). NASA MSL 'where' page checked: no coordinates in its text.

sites.notes: Mars target 2. Tile PG_Gale_CTX_3_3_AATE_20m.tif (20 m) chosen: covers the point; 4 km disk valid fraction 1.0 (>= 0.90 required). Extracted to data/raw/mars/gale/ctx_3_3/. Gale crater centre (Wikipedia -5.4, 137.8) not used.
sites.outcome_note: NASA: Curiosity landed on Mars on Aug. 6, 2012 and has been exploring Gale Crater since 2012.
sites.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia 'Bradbury Landing' coordinate template (-4.5895, 137.4417); the NASA MSL page read gives no coordinates.

sites.name: InSight landing site, Elysium Planitia

center_source.how: Golombek et al. 2020, Earth and Space Science: lander position 4.502384 N, 135.623447 E. SECONDARY: from a search snippet only; the paper (agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com) returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-14. NASA InSight page (science.nasa.gov/mission/insight/, read 2026-11-14) gives only 'centered at about 4.5 degrees north latitude and 135.9 degrees east longitude' (pre-landing target, not used).

sites.notes: Mars target. CTX DTM 20 m, 6 km remote window (not a whole-file download).
sites.outcome_note: NASA: InSight landed on Nov. 26, 2018 at 11:52:59 a.m. PT on Elysium Planitia.
sites.center_note: Secondary source: Golombek et al. 2020 via search snippet (paper not opened, publisher HTTP 403); the NASA page gives only the 135.9 E pre-landing target.

sites.name: Gusev crater, Spirit landing site (Columbia Memorial Station)

center_source.how: NASA science page 'In Depth: Spirit' (page dated Dec 19, 2024, read 2026-11-14), quoted: 'Landing coordinates were 14.5692 degrees south latitude and 175.4729 degrees east longitude.' PRIMARY.

sites.notes: Mars target. CTX DTM 20 m, 6 km remote window.
sites.outcome_note: NASA: 'The entire rover package hit the Martian surface at 20:35 PST Jan. 3, 2004' at Gusev crater.
sites.center_note: Primary: NASA science page quotes the landing coordinates directly.

sites.name: Utopia Planitia, Zhurong landing site (Tianwen-1)

center_source.how: SECONDARY: Li et al. 2022, Nature 610 (figure caption, via search snippet) and Ding et al. 2022, Nature Geoscience 15:171-176 (abstract, via snippet) both give 25.066 N, 109.925 E. The papers were not opened: nature.com redirects to a login page (2026-11-14). Wikipedia Tianwen-1 gives 25 deg 03 min 58 s N, 109 deg 55 min 30 s E (consistent).

sites.notes: Mars target. CTX DTM 20.73 m, 6 km remote window.
sites.outcome_note: Zhurong landed on Utopia Planitia in May 2021 and operated on the surface (Ding et al. 2022, read via snippet).
sites.center_note: Secondary source: two peer-reviewed papers read only via search snippets (Li et al. 2022; Ding et al. 2022), not opened; Wikipedia agrees.

sites.name: Oxia Planum, ExoMars Rosalind Franklin landing site (favoured ellipse)

center_source.how: SECONDARY: Wikipedia 'Rosalind Franklin (rover)' mirror: favoured Oxia Planum landing ellipse 18.20 N, 335.45 E (= -24.55). ESA primary not found (esa.int search returned no coordinates, 2026-11-14). Wikipedia plain centre 18.275 N, 335.368 E not used.

sites.notes: Mars target, future mission. CTX DTM 20.04 m, 6 km remote window. Landing year from an ESA-affiliated abstract, not an esa.int page.
sites.outcome_note: Planned, not flown: ESA-affiliated EPSC 2026 abstract (Sefton-Nash et al.) says the rover is 'on schedule for launch in the latter part of 2028 and to land at Oxia Planum in 2030'.
sites.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia mirror, favoured landing ellipse (not the plain centre); no ESA primary coordinate found.

sites.name: Apollo 17 landing site, Taurus-Littrow (control site)

center_source.how: NSSDC Apollo landing-site table, 'Lunar Module' row: 20.1911, 30.7723, planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421 (page read 2026-11-14). PRIMARY (NASA archive).

sites.notes: Moon control site. LROC NAC DTM 5 m, 6 km remote window.
sites.outcome_note: Apollo 17 landed in the Moon's Taurus-Littrow Valley in December 1972 (NASA: launch Dec. 7, 1972; splashdown Dec. 19, 1972).

sites.name: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus landing site, Malapert A area

center_source.how: NASA LRO release, Feb 26, 2024, read 2026-11-14: 'Odysseus came to rest at 80.13 degrees south latitude, 1.44 degrees east longitude, 8,461 feet (2,579 meters) elevation'. PRIMARY.

sites.notes: Moon target, tipped over on landing. LOLA 20 m polar LDEM, 6 km remote window. Centre near the north edge of the 80-90 S tile; check the edge margin.
sites.outcome_note: Odysseus came to rest on its side in Feb 2024: Intuitive Machines CEO Steve Altemus said at the Feb 23, 2024 briefing, 'we're tipped over' (NBC report of the briefing).
sites.center_note: Primary: NASA LRO release gives the resting coordinates. The tip-over statement is the company's, reported by news (NASA's release does not mention it).

sites.name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena landing site, Mons Mouton area

center_source.how: LROC 'IM-2 Landing Region' page (mirror lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1401, read 2026-11-14), Mark Robinson, 26 Feb 2025: 'intended landing site (-84.78°, 29.13°E)'. This is the INTENDED site, not the touchdown point. PRIMARY (NASA-funded LROC) for the intended site.

sites.notes: Moon target, tipped over on landing. LOLA 20 m polar LDEM, 6 km remote window. The 6 km disk is much wider than the touchdown offset.
sites.outcome_note: Athena 'hit the surface faster than intended and ended up on its side within a 20-meter diameter crater' (LROC, Mark Robinson, 10 Mar 2025).
sites.center_note: Primary: intended site from LROC. The LROC page gives no touchdown point; the 6 km disk covers it. Touchdown offset not measured here.
